# Neo.mjs v13.3.0 Release Notes

**Release Type:** Grid Fits Its Content, a focused features release: the first on the one-to-two-week cadence, with the package's entry points unchanged
**Stability:** Stable
**Upgrade Path:** A drop-in replacement for 13.2. Both new grid features are opt-in and the package's entry points are unchanged; see *Upgrading from 13.2* below.

> **TL;DR:** A grid with a fixed row height has to choose: clip long text, or make every row as tall as the longest one. In Neo.mjs 13.3, each row can fit its wrapped text instead, measured by the browser's own layout, and the row you are reading holds still while the heights arrive. Header menus filter the same grid by checked values, with counts that respect every other filter. Both features are opt-in; for everything else, 13.3 is a drop-in update.

## 📋 13.3 in 2 Minutes

**New to Neo.mjs?** It is an AI engineering team and the multi-threaded application engine that team builds, in sibling open-source repositories ([README](https://github.com/neomjs/neo#readme)). This note covers the engine. In the engine, your app's components, state and data stores run in a worker, the App Worker; the main thread applies DOM changes and answers layout questions, so your application logic stays off it.

**Who builds it:** AI maintainers from the Claude, GPT and Gemini model families, and one human maintainer, Tobi ([@tobiu](https://github.com/tobiu)); see [the team](https://github.com/neomjs/neo#the-maintainer-team). This release's pull requests came from Ada ([@neo-opus-ada](https://github.com/neo-opus-ada)), Grace ([@neo-opus-grace](https://github.com/neo-opus-grace)) and Vega ([@neo-opus-vega](https://github.com/neo-opus-vega)) on Claude, Euclid ([@neo-gpt](https://github.com/neo-gpt)) and Sophie ([@neo-gpt-sophie](https://github.com/neo-gpt-sophie)) on GPT, Julia ([@neo-gemini-pro](https://github.com/neo-gemini-pro)) on Gemini, and one outside contributor. The maintainers review each other across model families, every Engine pull request runs the tests its change can reach, and Tobi merged every pull request in this release except five automatic Dependabot bumps.

**The one line:** the grid fits its content.

**Two opt-in settings:**
1. **Content-sized rows** ([#19658](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658)). `contentSizedRows: true` sizes each row to its tallest wrapped cell, measured by the browser, and keeps locked columns aligned. The row you are reading holds still while measured heights replace estimates.
2. **Header menus** ([#19643](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19643)). `columnMenu: true` gives each column a value picker with search and live counts, opened by right-click, a hover arrow, the keyboard or touch. The counts respect the grid's other filters.

**Try it:** the [issues showcase](https://neomjs.com/examples/grid/issues/index.html) shows both on Neo's own 497 most recent issues; *What you can try* below walks through it.

**The limits:** content-sized rows are proven at 10k rows, and they size cells by their text, not by images or components. Header menus count local data only. Each chapter's *Honest bounds* says more.

**Under the hood:** every Engine pull request now runs the end-to-end tier that hosted CI used to skip.

**The scale:** 68 pull requests merged in `neomjs/neo` and 75 issues closed since 13.2.0 shipped on 2026-10-11. The *Full Changelog* lists them.

**Read for your work:** the grid chapters for text and filtering, *Tests that drive the real app* for how the engine is verified, *Upgrading from 13.2* if you ship the engine, and *For maintainers* if you cut releases.

## 📏 Content-sized rows: the grid fits its text

A buffered grid keeps a small pool of row elements and moves them over a large store as you scroll. To place row 5,000 and size the scrollbar, it needs every row's height, so until 13.3 it assumed one height for all of them: wrapped text was cut off, or every row was tall enough for the longest cell. Variable row heights had been on the grid's backlog since March ([#9495](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9495)). 13.3 lets a grid drop the assumption:

```javascript
{
    module          : GridContainer,
    contentSizedRows: true,
    store           : MainStore,
    columns         : [
        {dataField: 'title',   locked: 'start', text: 'Title',   width: 160, wrapText: true},
        {dataField: 'summary',                  text: 'Summary', width: 280, wrapText: true},
        {dataField: 'owner',                    text: 'Owner',   width: 110}
    ]
}
```

Each row takes the height of its tallest `wrapText` cell. A grid can lock columns at its start and end around a scrolling center, and all three regions share each row's height, so the locked columns stay aligned. Fixed height stays the default, and a fixed-height grid is unchanged.

<img width="100%" alt="The issues showcase in the light theme: every row as tall as its longest wrapped text, the title in the locked start column or the summary in the center, from two lines to four" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/main/resources_pub/website/release-notes/v13.3.0/grid-issues-light.png" />

### Measured by the browser, not predicted

In Neo.mjs, measuring the text is the hard part. The grid's logic runs in the App Worker, which has no DOM, and a height predicted from font metrics is only an estimate: fonts, scripts, zoom and CSS each move it. So the App Worker does not predict; it asks the browser. A hidden pre-render lays out a batch of cells with the grid's own cell CSS, and one layout pass yields every height, sent back in a single round trip. The engine already had both parts, rendering text into a hidden measuring element and reading many element sizes in one call, so the feature needed no text-layout library. Neo builds on its own primitives before it reaches for one ([the design discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18880598)).

A probe priced the pass at 300 cells: 3.6 ms in Chromium 153, and 4 ms in Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6 (medians of 7 runs). The worker-to-main round trip stayed under 0.1 ms.

### Keeping your place while heights arrive

Rows not yet measured start from an estimated height. When a measured height replaces an estimate above the row you are reading, everything below it would shift. 13.3 corrects the scroll position in the same update, so the visible row stays put ([#19674](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19674)), and a row reached by keyboard keeps its edge while the rows around it are measured ([#19699](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19699)). One row-geometry model per view, the height and offset of every row, drives scrolling, the scrollbar and keyboard navigation ([#19668](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19668)). The `AnimateRows` plugin's row animations do not run in this mode ([#19677](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19677)).

### Case study: one pixel between macOS and Linux

Every local run passed on macOS. In CI, on Linux, a row of the 10k example shrank from 62px to 43px the moment its column mounted. The hidden measuring cells kept a 1px right border that the displayed cells drop on a region's last column. Under CI's fallback font, which shares Arial's metrics, that one pixel wrapped the row's text to three lines in the hidden cell and two in the displayed one. The fix builds the hidden cells with the same last-column flag as the displayed ones, and a unit test compares a hidden cell's classes with its displayed cell's, so the two cannot drift apart again. Swept over five fonts, two runs each, no row changed ([#19704](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19704)).

That is the condition the design rests on: the measuring cells must match the displayed cells exactly. With that held, the heights are the browser's own layout, every font, script, zoom level and CSS rule included.

### Case study: a recycled row kept its previous record's height

On an early 100k-row draft of the content-sized example at 1400×900, jumping to row 99,996 and pressing ArrowDown four times left the last row 100px tall, while its text needed 81px. 100px was the height of the record that had last used that pooled row element. The engine's virtual DOM had moved on to the new record, the page's DOM had not yet, and nothing flagged the gap, so the measurement read the old text. Before the fix, 18 of 20 headless runs ended with the stale height; after it, none of 20. A cell is now read only once the DOM shows it ([#19692](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19692), [#19695](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19695)).

### The proof

The design discussion listed ten examples the feature had to handle. Each is now a named end-to-end test, checked against the browser's layout: a row must fit its tallest text plus the cell's padding and borders ([#19704](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19704)).

### Honest bounds

- Proven at 10k rows, not 100k. Past 2^23 px of scroll height, Chrome rounds scroll offsets to 2 px, and browsers cap element heights at different limits ([#19658](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658#issuecomment-6134339160)). Scaled scrolling beyond that is deferred.
- Cells size by their text. Images and components in cells, tree stores, remote data, and uniform or capped N-line modes are deferred.

## 🔽 Grid header menus: filter a column by its values

An engine user asked for a header menu whose first tool is a value picker with counts. 13.3 ships it, opt-in:

```javascript
{
    module    : GridContainer,
    columnMenu: true,
    columns   : [
        {dataField: 'firstname', text: 'Firstname'},
        {dataField: 'id',        text: 'Id', columnMenu: false}
    ]
}
```

Right-click a header, or use the arrow button that appears on hover or focus, Shift+F10, the ContextMenu key, or touch. One floating picker opens, with search, a count beside every value, and checkboxes that filter at once. The selection belongs to the store, so two grids on one store, or a header rebuilt later, show the same filter. Sorting, resizing and reordering keep their own paths ([#19711](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711)).

In the showcase: the Author menu with each author's issue count, then the Area menu searched for "Gri", with Grid checked and the grid down to its 71 Grid issues.

<img width="100%" alt="The showcase's Author menu, opened from the header's arrow: a search field above the authors' logins, each with its issue count, such as neo-opus-ada 159 and neo-opus-grace 130" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/main/resources_pub/website/release-notes/v13.3.0/grid-issues-menu-author.png" />

<img width="100%" alt="The Area menu searched for Gri, with Grid checked and a Clear button; the grid behind it shows only Grid issues, and the subtitle reads 71 of 497 issues" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/main/resources_pub/website/release-notes/v13.3.0/grid-issues-filtered.png" />

### Counts that respect the other filters

A value's count is how many rows hold it under every other active filter: check *Bug* in the Type menu, and the Area menu counts bugs only. The store counts its raw data in the App Worker, off the main thread. It writes nothing, builds no record instances, and neither removes nor reapplies a filter. On the 100k-record `bigData` store, sampled raw records stay unchanged through open, search and recount ([#19673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19673), [#19711](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711)). One Firstname count there takes 88–165 ms of worker CPU, and a recount after checking a value settles in 313 ms ([#19711](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711)).

### Whose filter is it?

The store used to find a filter by its property, and the first match won. A test run during the design showed what that would do to a menu: in two creation orders, the picker's filter and an application's own filter on the same field overwrote each other ([the test](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19646#discussioncomment-18880470)). Now `Collection` and `Filter` identify a filter by its owner's role and its field, so a menu's filter and your code's filter on the same field coexist. Looking a filter up by property alone still works for existing code ([#19673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19673)).

### Typed values

Options sort by their typed values: numbers by value (`1, 2, 10, 20, 100`), dates by time, each type in its own group, and text in natural order. Dates get locale-aware labels, and empty strings, `null` and `undefined` show as `(blank)`, `(null)` and `(undefined)` ([#19724](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19724)). Checking a value refreshes the open menu once.

A menu lists at most 1,000 unchecked values that match its search. On the id column of 100k records, a footer asks for a narrower search:

<img width="320" alt="The id column's menu at 100,000 rows, scrolled to its end: values up to 1000, each with a count of 1, then the footer 100,000 values match, narrow the search" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/main/resources_pub/website/release-notes/v13.3.0/grid-header-menu-refine.png" />

**The proof:** 19 end-to-end cases in five spec files drive the menus in a real browser.

### Honest bounds

- Opt-in by design. A grid without `columnMenu` renders its headers as before, and that is tested.
- Local data only: the counts read the store's local records. Remote, partial and tree stores are deferred.
- When a column's values cannot be counted, as with remote or tree data, data still loading, or values the picker cannot compare, the menu says so instead of guessing.
- The 100k timings come from one measurement, not a performance promise.
- Deferred: a grid-level search toolbar, exclusion mode, hide, lock and width commands, and a column chooser.

## 🧪 Tests that drive the real app

A green test suite proves only what it runs, and only against the app it actually drives. 13.3 closed a gap of each kind.

**The skipped tier.** Until 13.3, hosted CI skipped most of the engine's end-to-end tests: the ones that drive a running app inside its worker through the Neural Link, Neo's bridge into a live App Worker. 96 of 145 spec files never ran there ([the discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19599)), and a dock regression from [#19559](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19559) sat unseen on `dev` for about 14 hours, until a bisect found it.

Now every Engine pull request runs that tier, and a red blocks the merge ([#19705](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19705)). A change that cannot reach a spec's area runs a smaller smoke set. At the promotion, the tier was 266 tests on ten shards, all passing, one of them after a retry; its slowest step stayed under four minutes against a five-minute ceiling.

**It found engine bugs before it blocked anything.** First the tier ran only on `dev`, where a red stopped nothing, and measured its hosted time ([#19667](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19667)). It found three engine bugs, and each was fixed for its class:
- A component moved into another browser window could loop on a "mounted" promise left over from its earlier mount; this was the burn-in's most frequent failure. An unmounted component now hands out a pending promise ([#19689](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19689)).
- A tab strip collapses tabs that do not fit behind an overflow menu. It read a tab header destroyed mid-update as live, and logged its own teardown as a defect ([#19701](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19701)).
- Undoing the close of a popup window could leave its pane in neither window: a layout update from the main window ran about a second late and took the pane back. A layout update now stands down once a newer one has placed the pane ([#19703](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19703)).

### 🕵️ War Story: an async predicate that never waited

**Symptom.** While the header menu was being wired into the grid, a test that opened a fresh page of the bigData example sent its writes into an older session of the same example, one with header menus already on ([#19713](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19713)).

**Investigation.** The test fixture's `connectToApp` attaches a test to the page's App Worker, and it asked the page for that worker's id through `page.waitForFunction(async () => …)`. A probe on the pinned Playwright 1.63.0, against a page that sets a value after 1,500 ms:

| Predicate | Result |
|---|---|
| `async () => window.id ?? null` | `null` after 9 ms |
| `() => window.id ?? null` | `"ready"` after 1,492 ms |

**Culprit.** Playwright treats the async predicate's Promise as truthy, so the wait resolved on its first read and never polled. During bootstrap that read is `null`, and the fixture fell back to binding by app name, which resolves to the oldest session with that name. All 139 `connectToApp` calls pass a name, and the async predicate had been in the fixture since 2026-06-11 ([#12904](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/12904)).

**Fix the class.** `connectToApp` no longer binds by name ([#19715](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19715)). Given a name, it polls for the page's own App Worker id for up to 30 seconds and fails if none arrives; given an App Worker id, it binds that id. With the old read restored, a new test that first connects an older same-name session goes red.

**The portable lesson:** a `waitForFunction` predicate must return its value synchronously. An `async` predicate returns a Promise, which is truthy, so the wait ends at once.

## 🧰 Also in 13.3

- **Animated sorting moves each card once.** An animated component list moved its retained cards twice before settling on a new sort order; now they move straight to the latest order. The store marks the load a sort emits with `isSort: true`, so adding, removing or clearing cards still rebuilds the list at once ([#19717](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19717), [#19738](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19738), [#19752](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19752)).
- **Animated row sorting works again.** The grid's `AnimateRows` plugin predated the grid's pool of reusable rows, and it threw on every header sort and filter in its own example. It now moves each record from its old row position to its new one and fades in the records that enter. Rows transition only while they move, so scrolling never animates ([#6858](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/6858), [#19774](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19774)).
- **Locked columns follow the grid's settings.** Since locked columns got their own bodies and headers ([#9487](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9487)), those regions ignored the grid's `body` and `headerToolbar` configs: a locked column had no header filters, sorting options, row animation or modified-cell highlighting. They now carry them, and the animated sorting example locks its Id column to show its rows moving with the rest ([#19772](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19772), [#19777](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19777)).
- **Dock animations finish before a resize.** Dock layouts land their animated geometry with CSS transitions suppressed, so a native window resize reads the landed geometry ([#19708](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19708)).
- **The Workstation's film tour restores its saved two-window arrangement.** The Workstation is the multi-window Dock Layouts app from 13.2, and its film tour plays a scripted ten-scene walkthrough ([#19569](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19569), [#19731](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19731)). It was one of the two restore defects the roadmap carried; the other, [#16498](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/16498), stays open.
- **The Portal features the Workstation first** in every example mode ([#19641](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19641)). The Portal is the neomjs.com site. The npm 13.2.0 package still carries the old catalogs, so the site serves the correction from an overlay until 13.3.0 publishes it.
- **Both RealWorld apps boot again.** Their API singletons waited on a static `Base.on('ready')` that no class provides, so every singleton after the first threw. They now share one stored-token promise ([#19700](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19700)).
- **One grid keyboard-navigation failure stays open.** It is intermittent, and a failing run now captures the grid's state for diagnosis ([#19654](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19654)); the failure itself is [#19515](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19515).

### 🤝 From the community

@sloemo01, whose component spec for the Portal's CSS 3D cube appeared in 13.2, closed a ticket filed on 2023-02-17 ([#4069](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/4069)): reordering the items of a header toolbar should keep the gaps between them. The base sort zone's `switchItems` already did. [#19710](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19710) pins its gap math for the tab, grid and table headers, including the unequal-size case behind the ticket's 1.5px drift note.

## ▶️ What you can try

Open the [issues showcase](https://neomjs.com/examples/grid/issues/index.html), a grid of Neo's own 497 most recent issues:

1. Scroll. Each row is as tall as its title or summary needs, and the issue number and state stay aligned in their locked columns.
2. Untick *Content-sized rows* to see the same issues at a fixed height, then tick it again.
3. Open the Type menu from its header's arrow and check *Bug*: 270 of 497 issues remain. Then open the Area menu: its counts now count bugs only.
4. Switch to the dark theme with the button in the header.

On your own grid, set `contentSizedRows: true` on the grid and `wrapText: true` on its text columns, or `columnMenu: true` for the menus. For scale, open the [10k content-sized example](https://neomjs.com/examples/grid/contentSizedRows/index.html), or the [100k bigData example](https://neomjs.com/examples/grid/bigData/index.html) and tick *Column menus* on the Settings tab behind its ☰ button ([#19750](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19750)). From a checkout, after dependencies and fresh theme assets are in place, `npm run server-start -- --no-open` serves the same examples on the printed local port ([source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/tree/dev/examples/grid/issues)).

## 🧭 What comes next

Releases now come every one to two weeks. The cadence is fixed and the scope flexes: work that misses a window moves to the next release instead of holding the cut. 13.4's theme is not set yet; the [roadmap](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/ROADMAP.md) will name it. What 13.3 deferred is on record:

- **Content-sized rows:** more than 10k rows, images and components in cells, tree stores and remote data.
- **Header menus:** remote, partial and tree data, a grid-level search, exclusion mode, column commands and a column chooser.
- **Grids across windows:** a grid's locked or scrolling region moved into another browser window, with scrolling kept in sync on the main thread and keyboard navigation across the regions ([#9486](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9486)).
- **The engine:** a rebuilt middleware for server-side rendering ([#12964](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/12964)), and Pointer Events for drag and drop ([#17889](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17889)).

Found a gap, or built something with 13.3? Open an [issue](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues), start a [Discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions), or find us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/6p8paPq) and [Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/neomjs/shared_invite/zt-6c50ueeu-3E1~M4T9xkNnb~M_prEEOA).

## ⬆️ Upgrading from 13.2

**Nothing to change.** `package.json`'s `main`, `exports`, `bin`, `engines`, `type` and dependencies are unchanged since 13.2.0; besides the version, its only change is a devDependency, `neo-agent-skills` 0.1.39 → 0.1.41. Both grid features default off: `contentSizedRows: false` on the grid, and `columnMenu: false` on the grid with a per-column override.

**A reason not to wait: Chromium 156.** From Chromium 156, the version Playwright 1.64 ships, a grid's computed overflow changes from `hidden`/`hidden` to `hidden`/`clip`, and its automatic minimum height lets a flex-sized grid grow past the space its layout gives it. 13.3 sets `min-height: 0` on `.neo-grid-container`, so the grid's view does the scrolling again ([#19755](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19755), [#19690](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19690)). If you stay on 13.2 for now, add that rule to your own CSS.

**Public behaviour to check:**

| If your code… | In 13.3 | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| awaits `mountedPromise` on a component that is not mounted | the promise stays pending until the next mount; before, a promise settled by an earlier mount could be returned at once ([#19689](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19689)) | nothing, unless you relied on the early resolve |
| catches the rejection of a remote call whose target window is closing | the error keeps its `PortDisconnectedError` name and message, and adds the code `NEO_DEAD_PORT` and the target window id ([#19728](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19728)) | branch on the code if you need to |
| loads a Canvas renderer through `SharedCanvas` whose import can fail | the host no longer reports ready; it emits `canvasLoadFailed` ([#19734](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19734)) | listen for the event if you need a fallback |
| looks a store's filter up by property while a header menu filters the same field | each writer owns its filter by (role, dataField); the property-only lookup still returns the first match ([#19673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19673)) | nothing |

## 🛠️ For maintainers: a release is a pull request

*For the people who cut releases or contribute to Neo; skip it if you only use the engine.*

13.2.0's release script predated `dev`'s ruleset, which requires CodeQL and 18 checks on every pushed commit, so 13.2.0 shipped through a temporary bypass and by hand ([#19637](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19637)). Tobi then removed the bypass, since a standing one would let anything that authenticates as that account land on `dev` past CI, and asked for releases the AI maintainers can trigger without it. A release now takes the path every change takes ([#19653](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19653)):

1. `publish.mjs prepare` opens the release pull request, and `dev`'s required checks and CodeQL run on it.
2. Tobi merges it: the one human step.
3. `publish.mjs finish` squashes the merge onto `main` and creates the GitHub release.

Re-running a command resumes a phase that stopped, under three rules:
- **An unknown never passes for an absence.** A failed read used to become an empty list, `false` or a clean tree, so a 403 on the rules or a failed `git status` could have shown a green gate. A proven absence, such as a recognised 404 or an empty ref, is now kept apart from a failed observation, which stops the phase.
- **A ref is reused only when it belongs to this release.** An open release pull request with no local branch, or a release tag whose commit is unknown, now refuses instead of reading as *waiting* or *released*.
- **13.2.0 itself is refused,** because it was published outside this path.

**Honest bounds:** the path is proven against a scripted command boundary and a live rehearsal against the real rules, run as an account that cannot bypass them. 13.3.0's own cut is its first real run ([#19652](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19652)), and these notes claim a pull-request-gated cut only after `finish`, npm and neomjs.com have verified it. `finish` pushes the squash with `--no-verify` on purpose: the squash flattens every reviewed change since the last release into one commit, which the local pre-push check would reject by construction.

**The end-to-end retry bridge:** until 2026-10-25, a failing end-to-end test gets one retry in a fresh worker. Every run's receipt names each retried test, and the bridge expires on that date without anyone editing it ([#19682](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19682)). Each quarantined test names an owner and an exit, and goes stale after seven days.

## 📦 Full Changelog
